_meta.indication: Emergency contraceptive indicated for prevention of pregnancy following unprotected intercourse or a known or suspected contraceptive failure; not intended for routine use as a contraceptive

pivotal_trials.design: Prospective, open-label, single-arm, multicenter study conducted in 40 centers in the United States
pivotal_trials.population: Women 18 or greater years of age, with regular cycle length (24 to 35 days) presenting for emergency contraception between 48 and 120 hours of UPI
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Pregnancy rate (number of pregnancies after intake of emergency contraception divided by the total number of subjects having received emergency contraception)
pivotal_trials.n: 1,533 enrolled; 1,242 women aged 18 to 35 evaluated for efficacy
pivotal_trials.result: ella statistically significantly reduced the pregnancy rate from an expected rate of 5.5% to an observed rate of 2.2% (95% CI 1.5, 3.2) when taken 48 to 120 hours after unprotected intercourse

pivotal_trials.design: Prospective, multicenter, randomized, single-blind, parallel-group comparative trial of ulipristal acetate 30 mg versus levonorgestrel 1.5 mg, conducted in the US and Europe
pivotal_trials.population: Women 16 or greater years of age, with regular cycle length (24 to 35 days) presenting for emergency contraception within 120 hours of UPI
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Pregnancy rate; and non-inferiority of ulipristal acetate 30 mg versus levonorgestrel 1.5 mg within 72 hours of UPI
pivotal_trials.n: Total 2,221 (ulipristal 1,104; levonorgestrel 1,117); 844 women in the ella group aged 16-35 evaluated for efficacy (0-72 hours)
pivotal_trials.result: In the ella group (0-72 hours), 16 pregnancies in 844 women; pregnancy rate reduced from an expected 5.6% to an observed 1.9% (95% CI 1.1, 3.1)

key_safety: Most common adverse reactions (≥5%): headache (18%), abdominal pain (12%), nausea (12%), dysmenorrhea (9%), fatigue (6%) and dizziness (5%)
target_moa: Selective progesterone receptor modulator with antagonistic and partial agonistic effects; binds the human progesterone receptor and prevents progesterone from occupying it; the likely primary mechanism for emergency contraception is inhibition or delay of ovulation (postponement of follicular rupture)

rems.type: No postmarket risk evaluation and mitigation strategies are recommended

advisory_committee.vote: At a June 17, 2010 meeting, the Advisory Committee for Reproductive Health Drugs unanimously voted that there was sufficient safety and efficacy data to recommend marketing approval for emergency contraception up to 120 hours after unprotected intercourse

description.text: Clarified dosing instructions for initiating/resuming progestin-containing hormonal contraception no sooner than five days after ella intake following contraceptive failure

citations.quote: The edits reflect clarification of instructions for initiation and resumption of a progestin-containing hormonal contraception (COCs, progestin-only pill, and non-oral progestin-containing contraception) no sooner than five days after ella intake to apply to women using ulipristal acetate for a known or suspected contraceptive failure.

Application Type NDA
Application Number(s) 22-474
Priority or Standard Standard

summary.text: ella (ulipristal acetate) is a new molecular entity approved under a standard review NDA on the basis of two adequate and well-controlled Phase 3 trials; the Advisory Committee for Reproductive Health Drugs unanimously recommended approval on June 17, 2010, and no special expedited designations were applied.

citations.quote: Ulipristal acetate is a new molecular entity and is not currently available in any U.S. approved product.

Application Type NDA
Application Number(s) 22-474
Priority or Standard Standard

UA 30 mg tablet is an emergency contraceptive indicated for the prevention of pregnancy following unprotected intercourse or a known or suspected contraceptive failure. The efficacy portion of the Application is supported by two phase 3 clinical trials.

At a meeting held on June 17, 2010, the Advisory Committee for Reproductive Health Drugs unanimously voted that there was sufficient safety and efficacy data to recommend marketing approval for the indication of emergency contraception up to 120 hours after unprotected intercourse. I concur with the Committee's opinion and also recommend approval of ulipristal for the indication sought.

requirement.text: 1673-1: A prospective, observational pregnancy outcome study to include fetal and neonatal outcomes and maternal pregnancy complications following a pregnancy exposed to ulipristal acetate

citations.quote: 1673-1. A prospective, observational pregnancy outcome study to include fetal and neonatal outcomes and maternal pregnancy complications following a pregnancy exposed to ulipristal acetate (e.g., in case of inadvertent administration to a woman with an unrecognized pregnancy, or in case of emergency contraceptive failure). This study may be conducted by adding a US component to your planned European pregnancy outcome study.

requirement.text: 1673-2: A case-control study of pregnancy loss complications, conducted as an expansion of the pregnancy outcome study if a signal of concern is found

citations.quote: 1673-2. A case-control study of pregnancy loss complications. This study will be conducted as an expansion of the pregnancy outcome study (described under 1673-1), if a signal of concern regarding pregnancy complications is found in that study.

requirement.text: 1673-3: An observational study in adolescents focused on alterations to the menstrual cycle after use of ulipristal acetate, enrolling at least 50 completers under the age of 16

citations.quote: 1673-3. An observational study in adolescents, with particular focus on alterations to the menstrual cycle after use of ulipristal acetate. This study may be conducted by adding a US component to your planned UK/Sweden study of use in adolescents. The study should enroll at least 50 subjects (completers) under the age of 16 over the full study (these do not necessarily have to be US subjects).

requirement.text: 1673-4: A pharmacokinetic trial in lactating women evaluating the rate and extent of excretion of ulipristal acetate and its active metabolite into breast milk

citations.quote: 1673-4. A pharmacokinetic trial in lactating women, with evaluation of the rate and extent of excretion of ulipristal acetate and its active metabolite into breast milk. Your planned lactation trial to be conducted in Chile appears likely to fulfill this requirement.

requirement.text: 1673-5: To conduct an in vivo drug-drug interaction trial of ulipristal acetate with a CYP3A4 inducer

citations.quote: 1673-5. To conduct an in vivo drug-drug interaction trial of ulipristal acetate with a CYP3A4 inducer.
